pr.title: feat(coldstart): task-orchestrator HTTP-singleton MCP cutover + rollback docs
pr.body:
## Summary
- Replaces the per-client stdio launcher with a single HTTP singleton server per workspace.
- Updates `.mcp.json` task-orchestrator entry from `type: stdio` to `type: http`.
- Adds `scripts/mcp-wrappers/task-orchestrator-http-singleton.sh` — starts ONE `docker run -d --restart unless-stopped` container per workspace, exposing `MCP_TRANSPORT=http` on a deterministic port; idempotent (no-op if already running at correct SHA).
- Adds `scripts/mcp-wrappers/task-orchestrator-rollback-stdio.sh` — documented rollback path (stop HTTP container, revert .mcp.json to stdio, periodic `docker kill` prune advice).
- Adds `docs/03-reference/orchestrator-integration/http-singleton-cutover.md` — migration guide, port selection, rollback procedure, and the 2-session coexistence proof.

## Scope
Series: DMX-COLDSTART. Risk: HIGH. Layer: L2. Contract-sensitive transport change. Supervisor review required.

## Background
POC verified 2026-05-31: `MCP_TRANSPORT=http` + `MCP_PORT=<port>`, `POST http://localhost:<port>/mcp` returns HTTP 200 + 14-tool serverInfo (Streamable HTTP, `mcp-session-id` header). HTTP clients spawn ZERO launcher containers. Root cause of SQLite contention: stdio launcher spawns one `--rm` container per MCP client; under multi-client/retry churn, blocked-alive containers contend on shared WAL. HTTP singleton is ONE server/workspace — no contention.

## Tracer note
The PAL tracer stage must trace the stdio launcher's workspace-root resolution (lines 55-80 of task-orchestrator-current-stdio.sh), singleton-enforcement logic (lines 128-160), and data_dir derivation (line 107) before any implementation begins. Transport change must carry over the same workspace_id computation and data_dir mount path.

## Validation
- Two concurrent mock sessions connect to HTTP endpoint; neither kills the other.
- `docker ps` shows exactly ONE task-orchestrator container per workspace after cutover.
- `docker kill` of the HTTP singleton causes .mcp.json clients to reconnect on next invocation.
- Rollback: revert .mcp.json + run rollback script → stdio behavior restored.
Capture proof under proof/TP-DMX-COLDSTART-ORCH-HTTP-CUTOVER-109/PROOF.json.

## NOT_RUN
- Live multi-session test with real Claude Code sessions (requires operator to run manually; script test covers the container lifecycle).
- Port selection for team environments (documented as UNKNOWN pending CS-08 port policy).

Read `.mcp.json` (line 25: type=stdio, command, env vars). Read `.claude/hooks/mcp_health_probe.py` to understand how the health probe detects the transport type. Read `docs/03-reference/orchestrator-integration/plugin-hooks-port.md` for prior HTTP context. Identify the exact IMAGE SHA pinned in the stdio script (v3.8.0 at line 4) — confirm it supports http transport (POC-verified). Run PAL tracer on the stdio flow before coding.

data_dir path formula is confirmed: ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/dopemux-mission-control/task-orchestrator/<workspace_id>.
IMAGE SHA (ghcr.io/jpicklyk/task-orchestrator@sha256:e47ed00aa...) is confirmed to support MCP_TRANSPORT=http per POC.
mcp_health_probe.py transport-detection logic is noted — ensure probe works with http transport.
Any UNKNOWN authority gaps (e.g., port assignment policy, multi-host scenarios) are recorded explicitly.
PAL tracer invoked on the stdio singleton-enforcement block before proceeding to S2.

steps.task: Implement the HTTP singleton cutover: (1) Author `scripts/mcp-wrappers/task-orchestrator-http-singleton.sh` — derives workspace_id using the SAME algorithm as the stdio script (ensure exact parity); selects a deterministic port (default 7890, overridable via TASK_ORCHESTRATOR_HTTP_PORT env); checks if a container with the correct name AND image SHA is already running (idempotent, no-op if healthy); otherwise removes any stale container by name or data_dir mount, then runs `docker run -d --restart unless-stopped --name <container_name> -p 127.0.0.1:<port>:<port> -v <data_dir>:/app/data -e MCP_TRANSPORT=http -e MCP_PORT=<port> -e DATABASE_PATH=/app/data/current-tasks.db -e USE_FLYWAY=true -v <config>:/project/.taskorchestrator:ro <IMAGE> java ...`. Mounts logback.xml. (2) Author `scripts/mcp-wrappers/task-orchestrator-rollback-stdio.sh` — documented rollback: kill HTTP container, guidance to revert .mcp.json entry to stdio. (3) Update `.mcp.json` task-orchestrator entry: change `type` from `stdio` to `http`, set `url` to `http://127.0.0.1:${TASK_ORCHESTRATOR_HTTP_PORT:-7890}/mcp`, remove `command` and `args` (not valid for http type), preserve `env` block. (4) Author migration runbook `docs/03-reference/orchestrator-integration/http-singleton-cutover.md` with: pre-cutover checklist, cutover steps, rollback steps, 2-session coexistence test procedure.
requirements: HTTP singleton script must derive workspace_id identically to the stdio script — share the derivation logic, do not re-implement it divergently.
Script must be idempotent: running it twice when a healthy container already exists is a no-op.
data_dir mount path must be IDENTICAL to what the stdio script would use for the same workspace.
Rollback script must be executable and tested as a dry-run.
